dimensions.assessment: Targets foreign persons and entities engaged in religious persecution in occupied Ukraine, while involving multiple U.S. federal departments and congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: To require the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense to jointly submit a report on efforts by the Government of the Russian Federation to persecute, suppress, discriminate, or otherwise violate the religious freedoms of Ukraine

dimensions.assessment: Imposes mandatory asset-blocking and other federal sanctions on designated foreign individuals and entities.
dimensions.evidence: the President shall impose applicable sanctions with respect to each such person pursuant to the authorities and procedures set forth in the applicable regulations

dimensions.assessment: No specific direct appropriations are stated, with costs limited to administrative reporting.
Requires new interagency reporting mechanisms, presidential certifications, and the enforcement of statutory sanctions.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, and annually thereafter for 3 years, the Secretary of State and Secretary of Defense... shall jointly submit... a report

dimensions.assessment: Requires annual reports for a duration of three years, alongside ongoing sanctions enforcement until modified.

missing_information: Exact number of individuals or entities that will ultimately be sanctioned
Specific cost estimates for preparing the required federal reports
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates joint executive branch reporting on religious freedom violations in Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine and requires the imposition of sanctions on certified foreign persons.
